what: Live proof that a deferred Taskfold attaches without consent, keeps its `tasks` tool, and runs no model call until consent arrives.
how: One Pi-Bolt RPC session (deepseek/deepseek-flash, ACCORDION_AUTO_ARM=1, defaultConductor taskfold, debug on). Phase A ran a prompt that calls `tasks` with no privacyConsent in the settings file; then `privacyConsent.taskfold-chat-v1` was written into the same file, the runtime adopted it, and phase B sent one user message.

notices: Taskfold: deterministic tools are active now; its classifier and chat routing wait for a one-time consent.
phaseA.status: accordion · Taskfold · eager · deterministic tooling active; classifier: awaiting consent.

phaseB.note: The classifier request is the gate lifting; the queued-drain path itself is covered by the unit test, because the phase-A user message was the session's opening message and is never classified.

conclusion: Consent gates only model-backed work: the deterministic tool worked immediately, and the first model call happened after consent arrived, never before.
